clue.text: Dating seemed inappropriate with the prospect of attraction gone

definitions.text: with the prospect of attraction gone

indicators.note: something inappropriate is out of place, so the letters of the two words are put out of their places and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone decides a date would be unsuitable once the spark between them has faded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriate' rearranges the twelve letters of 'Dating seemed'. 'Attraction' in the surface is romantic; in the definition it is magnetic pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagnetised object has lost its magnetism, so it can no longer pull iron towards it.

clue.text: Duke was uncomfortable being deposed

parts.note: itched means felt an irritation

explanation.surface: A nobleman felt uneasy when he was being removed from power.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch someone is to get rid of them, as a deposed ruler is removed.

clue.text: Dispose of what's to be sold dishonestly after a short time?

indicators.note: the dishonest sale comes after the short time, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: a mo is a moment
to sell someone a pup is to swindle them with something worthless

explanation.surface: A crook gets rid of stolen goods quickly after a brief wait.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to finish off or deal with what remains, disposing of it.

clue.text: Impudence associated with Russian ruler having time to jaunt

parts.note: gall is cheek or impudence
Ivan was the name of several tsars, such as Ivan the Terrible

explanation.surface: A cheeky tsar finds time for a pleasure trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to go about looking for fun, which is to jaunt.

clue.text: Good English used by the person who needs it is an advantage

parts.note: an editor, ED for short, is the person who needs good English

explanation.surface: Writing well in English gives anyone who needs it a head start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' just places ED beside GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an edge over others means holding a slight lead or superiority.

clue.text: Intern at work getting source of company information?

indicators.note: letters set to work are put into a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainee on the job is given a company briefing.
explanation.definitionFit: An intranet is a private internal network carrying a firm's documents for its staff.

clue.text: Bush? Bush GHW rather than GW

definitions.meaning: a shrub of the genus Sambucus, with white flowers and black berries
George H W Bush was the father of George W Bush, so the older of the two

explanation.surface: A query about the US presidents named Bush: the father, not the son.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub Sambucus is a bush; the father of two people sharing a name is the senior one.

clue.text: Skilful manoeuvring of old couple in parting of the ways

indicators.note: the old couple sits in the split in the road, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a fork is where a road divides
a couple is two

explanation.surface: An elderly pair dodge cleverly where the road divides.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwork is nimble handling of a situation, like a boxer's or dancer's agile feet.

clue.text: Band makes second journey across Austria

indicators.note: the long journey reaches across the country's letter, so it goes around it

parts.note: a trek is a long journey
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A music group takes a second tour through Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a stripe or narrow line of colour, which is a band.

clue.text: Spooner's to go to bed the worse for drink? Excellent!

indicators.note: the clue credits the phrase to Dr Spooner, so the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: to flop is to collapse into bed, exhausted
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk boasts that tumbling into bed tipsy is a fine idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds FL and T of the two words gives the hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest class, which is an exclamation of approval like excellent.

clue.text: Legal claim? Abandon it if powerless

indicators.note: without power means the letter standing for power, P, is removed from the phrase

parts.note: to drop something is to abandon it

explanation.surface: Advice to give up a lawsuit if you have no leverage.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the usual abbreviation for power; taking it from DROPIT leaves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A droit is a right or due in law, the thing a person may lawfully claim.

clue.text: Rebel beginning to cheer, confused type

parts.note: a cheer begins with 'hip', as in hip hip hooray
pie is the printers' term for type that has been jumbled up

explanation.surface: A rebel starts to applaud, being a muddled sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' is printing type, not a kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippie of the 1960s counterculture rejected conventional society, a kind of rebel.

clue.text: Cloth being pulled round by bad person — shortly it results in strangulation

indicators.note: turning the word for the cloth round means its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word for the bad person is dropped

parts.note: a rotter is a nasty, unpleasant person

explanation.surface: A villain pulls a piece of fabric tight round someone's neck, choking them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it results in strangulation' defines the weapon by its effect; 'shortly' signals a cut-off final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotte is a wire or cord used to choke a victim, so its use ends in strangling.

clue.text: Money anguish as some might say

indicators.note: the word is pronounced in a way some speakers would, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: dolour is a literary word for grief or anguish

explanation.surface: Money troubles bring anguish, or so some people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is the currency of the USA and many other countries.

clue.text: Road around America descending to northern city

indicators.note: the road goes round the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

indicators.note: in a down entry, America comes down to the next letter, which follows it

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A route through America heads north towards a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descending to' works because this is a down entry: America comes just above the northern letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is a Swiss city on Lake Geneva.

clue.text: Stop awkward load crashing into platform

indicators.note: the jumbled load breaks into the platform, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: a deck is a platform, as on a ship

indicators.note: an awkward load is badly arranged, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A clumsy cargo smashes onto a platform and everything comes to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a standstill where neither side can move, a complete stop.

clue.text: Mark to take last breath finding fault audibly?

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the entry

parts.words: to take last breath finding fault
parts.note: to die (take one's last breath) a critic (one who finds fault)

explanation.surface: Someone complains right up to their dying breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is a mark, such as an accent, added to a letter.

clue.text: Guide turning up in the morning, protector of treasure going about

indicators.note: the treasure guardian goes about the other piece, so it encloses it

parts.note: in legend a dragon guards a hoard of treasure

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: AM means in the morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A guide arrives early, while a fierce guardian of riches prowls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses the morning abbreviation, since in a down entry up means bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in Arabic, Turkish or Persian-speaking lands.

clue.text: Grumbles from a hundred country folk threatened by saboteurs?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
hunt saboteurs disrupt fox hunts, so the people they threaten are those who ride with the hunt

explanation.surface: Rural people complain about the activists who disrupt their sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunt saboteurs are British activists who disrupt fox hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: To chunter is to mutter or complain in a low voice, a British colloquial verb.

clue.text: Plate in Italian city church placed high up

indicators.note: in a down entry the church comes high up, above the city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A dish in a Roman church stands on a high shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium plating, so to chrome is to plate.

clue.text: Group together to get rid of bishop, creating fuss

indicators.note: getting rid of means the letter for the churchman is removed

parts.note: to bracket things is to group them together
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: People unite to oust a church leader, causing a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud noise or commotion, a synonym of fuss.

clue.text: Enzyme makes journeys inside by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase is heard, so its sound gives the spelling entered

parts.note: trips in: takes journeys indoors

explanation.surface: A digestive protein travels about inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Trypsin is a digestive protein from the pancreas that breaks down proteins.

clue.text: A tedious occupation in eggs — one's driven mad with this?

indicators.note: the dull task sits in the word for fish eggs, so it goes inside

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs of a fish
a drag is a boring chore

explanation.surface: A dull job surrounded by eggs drives someone crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven' is literal: the anger comes on while driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is violent anger at the wheel, so a motorist is made furious by it.

clue.text: Herb that is buried under stuff

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece buried under the other comes below it

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A plant lies buried beneath some material.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramie is an Asian plant of the nettle family grown for its fibre.

clue.text: Ingenious rule to get small-minded about

indicators.note: the small-minded word goes about the letter, so it sits around it

parts.note: petty means small-minded

explanation.surface: A clever regulation is spoiled by narrow-minded people around it.
explanation.definitionFit: In an old sense pretty means clever or skilful, as in a pretty trick.

clue.text: Sensualist finally gets excited when it's revealed?

definitions.text: Sensualist finally gets excited when it's revealed?

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word for the pleasure-seeker

parts.note: high means elated or excited

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is thrilled when some flesh is on show.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the leg's upper part, which excites a sensualist when exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper leg, when glimpsed, stirs the sensualist the clue describes.

clue.text: Last stand made by teetotaller avoiding pint?

indicators.note: the pint avoids the abstainer, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a pint of bitter is a common pub order
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal or teetotaller

explanation.surface: A non-drinker making a final stand by refusing a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale; removing TT leaves BIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the stand on which a coffin rests, its final resting place before burial.

clue.text: Note unrevised after it's gone over

indicators.note: going over the word backwards leaves it unchanged, so it reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A memo that remains unchanged even after it has been checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over' sounds like checking a note; here it means read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth half a semibreve, a half note.

clue.text: Defends home volunteers being brought into Scottish farm

indicators.note: the two pieces are brought inside the word for the farm

parts.note: mains is a Scottish word for the farm attached to a mansion
in means at home
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers garrison a Highland farmhouse to protect it.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a position is to defend or uphold it.

clue.text: Characters going wild in London cheer a singer-songwriter

indicators.note: letters going wild run riot, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crowd in the capital roars wildly for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Cohen was the Canadian singer-songwriter behind Suzanne and Hallelujah.
